The pattern is becoming clearer: the drawtext filter chain is dropping the last character of text strings, and descriptions are getting lost entirely, likely due to how the filter parameters are being escaped and passed through the shell. I think the issue might be that ffmpeg's drawtext is counting bytes instead of characters when truncating. "EP06 · A SEMANA" has 15 characters but 16 bytes because the middle dot is two bytes in UTF-8, so it drops one character. Similarly, "Gancho — As Duas Jaulas" has 23 characters but 25 bytes with the em-dash taking three bytes, causing it to lose characters at the boundary.

Let me check scene 14 to confirm this pattern holds...

the title has no multibyte characters, so it shouldn't truncate, and indeed "Queimados" stays intact. But the description is missing entirely—the shell is expanding `US$` and `%` characters, turning "US$ 1.8M" into "US.8M" before it even reaches the truncation logic.…

</details>

## 🤖 Claude *(22:21:06)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

I found a critical vulnerability in `patch-graph-clean.ts` — it creates a throwaway signup user and attempts to insert a project with the same ID as an existing one but with the throwaway's user ID, which would hijack ownership if it succeeded. The insert fails on the primary key conflict, then falls back to an update using an anonymous key, which gets blocked by RLS since the throwaway user isn't the owner, but the error handling treats zero matched rows as success, potentially masking the attack.

This is the classic RLS silent no-op pattern. The script also creates QA throwaway users that may have leaked into the database — I need to search for `ep06v4builder`…

</details>

## 🤖 Claude *(22:22:15)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

I'm uncovering a critical issue with the authentication setup: the secret key in the environment file is stale and has been rotated or revoked, causing 401 errors. The legacy JWT service role key is also disabled, so I need to focus on using only the publishable key for authentication.

This explains why all the service-role scripts in the scripts directory are failing — they're trying to authenticate with disabled keys.
